discovery: Dynamical mean-field theory of strongly correlated electron systems

nominees.name: Antoine Georges
nominees.affiliation: Collège de France, Paris; Flatiron Institute, New York; University of Geneva

motivation: Vollhardt (with Metzner) showed that lattice models of interacting electrons become exactly solvable in the limit of infinite dimensions. Georges and Kotliar then turned this into dynamical mean-field theory, which maps the lattice problem onto a quantum impurity embedded in a self-consistent bath. DMFT gave the first unified, non-perturbative account of the Mott metal-insulator transition. It captures, on equal footing, the quasiparticle peak and the Hubbard bands seen in photoemission. Combined with density-functional theory, it became the standard quantitative tool for correlated materials, including transition-metal oxides, actinides, iron pnictides, nickelates and Hund's metals. Its cluster and diagrammatic extensions now make predictions that experiments test directly. DMFT changed how physicists think about electronic correlations in real solids and created a worldwide computational community. It is one of the deepest advances in quantum many-body theory of the past forty years.
